data.content_ref: inline:SRC_001 asserts the panel's reliability 'stems from the additive probability of detection: the likelihood that at least one panelist flags a checklist item that the expert intuitively skipped.' This posits a causal mechanism (independent detection probabilities compounding across panelists) but never addresses the problem's requirement to 'identify what evidence within a single evaluation would distinguish a genuine reliability gain from mere checklist compliance that happens to track the right answer.' The additive-detection mechanism would predict panelists independently flagging different items (high inter-rater dispersion on *which* items are flagged). If instead all panelists tick the same items in lockstep, the 'additive probability' mechanism is not operating — agreement is driven by shared checklist structure, not independent detection. SRC_001 fails to specify this distinguishing evidence, leaving the causal mechanism untestable against the compliance-vs-gain distinction the problem demands.
